title: Nondiscrimination Requirements
summary: The NCUA Board (Board) is publishing this final rule to remove a redundant and outdated regulation regarding nondiscrimination in lending. The regulation was intended to summarize the Fair Housing Act (FHA) prohibitions on discrimination related to real estate related loans, appraisals, and advertising. The Board's last substantive amendment to the regulation was finalized in 2001. Thus, the regulation does not reflect all case law or regulatory developments under the FHA, a statute that primarily falls under the jurisdiction of the Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) and continues to apply to federal credit unions (FCUs) regardless of this regulation. For these reasons, the Board is removing the regulation in its entirety.

title: Restoring Flexibility To Support Head Start Program Access
issuer: Health and Human Services Department; Children and Families Administration
summary: In this final rule, the Administration for Children and Families (ACF) removes requirements from the Head Start Program Performance Standards (Performance Standards) to restore local flexibility to Head Start programs and improve access to quality services. Specifically, this final rule removes requirements related to wages and benefits that the Administration believes are not in line with the plain language of the Head Start Act and are costly and overly prescriptive for Head Start programs and staff. ACF estimates these changes will result in over $2 billion in future cost savings for Head Start programs. The rescissions in this final rule impact the costliest parts of the final rule published by the Office of Head Start (OHS) in 2024, Supporting the Head Start Workforce and Consistent Quality Programming.

title: Fisheries of the Exclusive Economic Zone off Alaska; Pelagic Trawl Gear Definition
issuer: Commerce Department; National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
summary: NMFS proposes regulations to revise the regulatory definition of authorized fishing gear, including the definition of pelagic trawl gear, and the gear limitations for pelagic trawl gear, applicable to vessels in the exclusive economic zone (EEZ) off Alaska. This action is necessary to clearly allow the use of certain common components in codends and bycatch reduction devices, and to remove an outdated limitation on the use of parallel line trawls. This action is expected to provide additional flexibility and promote innovations in pelagic trawl gear design, which may reduce environmental impacts while maintaining efficient fishing operations. This action is intended to promote the goals and objectives of the Magnuson-Stevens Fishery Conservation and Management Act (Magnuson-Stevens Act), the Fishery Management Plan (FMP) for Groundfish of the Gulf of Alaska Management Area (GOA FMP) and the FMP for Groundfish of the Bering Sea and Aleutian Islands Management Area (BSAI FMP), and other applicable laws.

title: Air Plan Approval; AK; Fairbanks PM2.5 Boundary Redesignation and Clean Data Determination
summary: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing to approve a request from Alaska to revise the boundary designation of the existing Fairbanks North Star Borough nonattainment area for the 2006 primary 24-hour fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) National Ambient Air Quality Standard (NAAQS). The EPA is proposing to split the existing nonattainment area into two distinct nonattainment areas, an area covering Fairbanks and the Goldstream Valley, and an area covering North Pole. The proposed new areas cover the same geographic area as the existing area. The EPA is also proposing to issue a clean data determination (CDD), for the proposed Fairbanks and Goldstream Valley area ("proposed Fairbanks nonattainment area") based on a determination that the area is attaining the 2006 PM 2.5 NAAQS. If the EPA finalizes this CDD, certain Clean Air Act (CAA) requirements that apply to the proposed Fairbanks nonattainment area will be suspended for so long as the area continues to meet the 2006 24-hour PM 2.5 NAAQS. The EPA is taking this action pursuant to Clean Air Act sections 107, 110, 172, and 189.

This proposed AD would require repetitively inspecting the TR drive shaft; repetitively inspecting the exterior of the Air Comm Corporation (ACC) condenser duct assembly (duct assembly); repetitively inspecting (using a borescope) the interior of the ACC duct assembly; and depending on the results of these inspections, replacing certain parts. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-24-01, the manufacturer determined the applicable service information was missing procedures for the tinted windows. This proposed AD would require the same actions as AD 2025-24-01 and would additionally require new actions to include helicopters with the modification of tinted windows.
